templates.description: Direct cost and expectation pass-through across production inputs, headline consumer prices, and nominal wage demands.
Policy rate hikes tighten bank credit standards and debt-service burdens, cooling investment and core inflation after multi-quarter lag.
Energy, shipping, and tariff shocks raise import landed costs and propagate into core goods inflation and margin compression.
Fiscal stimulus expands aggregate demand more strongly when economic slack or binding monetary constraints prevent crowding out.
Persistent above-target headline inflation crosses salience thresholds, shifting long-run wage-price setting into a high-inflation regime.
